subject: biology
title: Genetic variants and mutations
key_idea: A **mutation** is a change in DNA. In coding DNA it can change the amino acids, so the protein has a different shape and may not work. In non-coding DNA it can change how much of a protein is made. Either way, the phenotype can change.

blocks.text: A mutation is a change in the DNA. This section covers what causes mutations and where in the DNA they can happen.

items.meaning: A change in the DNA, for example in the base sequence of a gene.
A different version of a section of DNA, which has arisen by mutation.
The parts of DNA that code for the amino acids of a protein.
The parts of DNA that do not code for a protein. Only about 1% of human DNA codes for proteins.

items: Mutations can happen when the genetic material is copied and there is an error.
Ultraviolet (UV) and other ionising radiation can cause mutations in skin cells, which can lead to cancer.
Most mutations do not change the protein, or change it only slightly.
Very rarely a mutation changes the protein enough to give a new **phenotype**.
A mutation is a change in DNA.
It can be in coding DNA or in non-coding DNA.
Copying errors and radiation can cause mutations.

blocks.text: A mutation in coding DNA changes the code for the protein. That can change the protein's shape and its job.

items.text: One base is changed, or extra bases are inserted into the gene.
The mRNA has a different sequence, so a codon is different.
A different amino acid is added, so the order of amino acids is different.
The shape changes. An enzyme's active site may no longer fit its substrate.
The protein no longer does its job properly.

items: A change from the codon CAG to GAG changes the amino acid from Gln to Glu.
Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a mutation in the gene for haemoglobin. The abnormal haemoglobin can alter the shape of red blood cells, so less oxygen reaches cells for respiration.
In beta thalassaemia, extra bases are inserted into the haemoglobin gene. The order of the triplets changes, so a different haemoglobin protein is made.
A change in coding DNA can change the order of amino acids.
A different order changes the protein's shape, and so its function.
A faulty enzyme may have an active site that its substrate cannot fit.

blocks.text: Non-coding DNA does not code for amino acids. It still matters, because it controls whether a gene is switched on.

items: Non-coding DNA can **switch genes on and off**. This is called controlling gene expression.
In transcription, RNA polymerase binds to non-coding DNA at the start of a gene.
A mutation here can mean RNA polymerase binds less well, or cannot bind.
Then less mRNA is made, or none, so **less protein** is made.
The amino acid sequence of the protein is not changed. The amount of protein is.

diagram.alt: Sort each effect into a mutation in coding DNA or a mutation in non-coding DNA.

items.text: The order of amino acids changes
The protein folds into a different shape
An enzyme's active site changes shape
A different amino acid is added to the protein
The same protein is made, but less of it
A gene is switched on or off differently

diagram.prompt: Which type of mutation causes this effect?

items: Non-coding DNA can switch genes on and off.
A mutation in it can change how much protein is made.
A mutation in coding DNA changes the protein itself.

checks.a: A change in the DNA (for example a change in the base sequence of a gene).

checks.q: Explain how a change in one amino acid in an enzyme could stop the enzyme working.
checks.a: A different protein shape is made. The active site is changed, so the substrate does not fit or bind.

worked_example.question:
One of the genes codes for an enzyme used in fat metabolism. A mutation in this gene causes a reduction in milk fat. The mutation changes one amino acid in the enzyme molecule.

Explain how a change in one amino acid in an enzyme molecule could stop the enzyme working.
answer_points: A different protein is made (the enzyme has a different shape or 3-D structure).
The active site is changed.
So the substrate does not fit or bind (an enzyme-substrate complex cannot form).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link. Do not write that the enzyme is denatured.

worked_example.question:
A gene coding for a protein has two alleles.

The first 5 codons of an mRNA strand for these alleles are:
Allele 1 - AUG CCA CAG GAG UUC
Allele 2 - AUG CCA GAG GAG UUC

Allele 2 has a mutation.

The amino acid for each codon is: AUG = Met, CCA = Pro, CAG = Gln, GAG = Glu, UUC = Phe.

Explain how the mutation in allele 2 could affect the functioning of this protein.
answer_points: The mutation changes the third codon from CAG to GAG (the 7th base is now G instead of C).
This changes the amino acid from Gln to Glu, so the sequence of amino acids is different.
The protein folds differently (the active site has a different shape), which affects its function.
worked_example.tip: Any three of the four points score. Work along the codons to find the one that differs.

worked_example.question:
Wolfram's Syndrome is a genetic disorder.
It is caused by a recessive allele (n).
In people with Wolfram's syndrome, a protein does not function correctly.

Explain how a change in an allele can stop a protein functioning correctly.
answer_points: There is a change in the base sequence of the DNA.
This changes the order of amino acids.
The shape of the protein changes.
The shape is no longer suited to its function, for example a change in an enzyme's active site shape.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link in the chain. Write them in order.

worked_example.question:
Complete the sentences about drug resistance and genetic variation by writing a suitable word or phrase in the spaces provided.

Bacteria can be killed by drugs called ______. The development of strains of bacteria that are resistant to these drugs is an example of ______ selection.

Resistant strains of bacteria have gene mutations that enable them to survive drug treatment.

Gene mutations are caused by random changes in the ______ of bases in DNA and result in the formation of new ______ in the bacteria. Mutation rates can be increased by ______ radiation and some chemicals.

In animals and plants, another source of genetic variation is a type of nuclear division called ______.
answer_points: Drugs that kill bacteria: antibiotics.
Resistance is an example of natural selection.
Random changes in the sequence of bases in DNA.
Mutations form new alleles.
Mutation rates are increased by ionising radiation and some chemicals.
Another source of genetic variation: meiosis.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each missing word or phrase.

items: A **mutation** is a genetic change.
(Supplement) A **gene mutation** is a random change in the base sequence of DNA.
Mutation is the way new **alleles** are formed.
Ionising radiation and some chemicals increase the rate of mutation.

worked_example.question:
Cells use genetic information when carrying out protein synthesis.

Explain why a change in the sequence of bases in the DNA does not always result in a change in enzyme function.
answer_points: Different codons (sequences of bases) may code for the same amino acid.
So there is no change in the protein or the enzyme.
The change may not affect the shape or bonding of the enzyme, so the active site still binds to the substrate.
The allele may be recessive and so not expressed.
The change may be in non-coding DNA.
worked_example.tip: Any three points score the three marks.

items: A mutation is a **rare**, random change in genetic material. It can be inherited.
Ionising radiation, such as gamma rays, X-rays and ultraviolet rays, increases the number of mutations.
Some **chemical mutagens**, such as chemicals in tobacco smoke, also increase the number of mutations.
Most mutations have no effect on the phenotype, some have a small effect and rarely one has a significant effect.
